title: Why some knots hold and others fail
text: Sailors {{1}} argued about knots for centuries, {{2}} the science of why a knot holds lagged far behind the craft of tying one. {{3}} was not until 2020 {{4}} mathematicians published a full theory of knot strength, simulating millions of virtual ropes {{5}} crossings and tangle history could be computed. The model confirmed the folklore: the {{6}} strands cross and jam, the harder the knot is to pull apart, and every extra crossing multiplies {{7}}. The mathematics will not help anyone tie a shoelace faster, {{8}} it finally explains why the granny knot betrays you under load and the reef knot does not.

gaps.explanation: Present perfect with a plural subject: have argued.

gaps.hint: conjunction: for centuries, ___ the science lagged
gaps.explanation: Contrast between craft and science: yet.
'It was not until X that…' — the fixed cleft frame.
The second half of the 'not until' cleft: that.

gaps.hint: relative: ropes ___ crossings could be computed
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the ropes to their crossings.

gaps.hint: adverb: the ___ strands cross and jam
gaps.explanation: 'The more … the harder …' — the double comparative.
Object pronoun referring to the holding power: multiplies it.
Contrast between practical use and explanation: but.
